messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Label reordering in color scales?
parts:
Hi all -

I just noticed something when using scale_colour_identity which I had assumed worked before, but appears not only to not work in scale_colour_identity, but also in the more basic scale_colour_discrete, so I assume it doesn't work in general.

The quirk comes when you give the labeler (or, I suppose, any other argument as well) a named vector and expect the scaling function to check the labels with the data values.   Here's an example :

df <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10, z = factor(rep(1:2, each = 5)))

ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = z), data = df) + 
  geom_point()

  

ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = z), data = df) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = c('1' = 'One', '2' = 'Two'))    

ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = z), data = df) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = c('2' = 'Two', '1' = 'One'))    

While no warning or error flags the mislabeling, the fact that you are giving scale_colour_discrete the named vector doesn't seem to matter; what matters is the order.  

Strangely enough, if you play with the values, Hadley gives an example under http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/scale_manual.html which does work correctly (which led me to believe it worked for other arguments as well) :

p <- qplot(mpg, wt, data = mtcars, colour = factor(cyl))
p
p + scale_colour_manual(values = c('6' = 'green', '8' = 'red', '4' = 'blue'))
p + scale_colour_manual(values = c('8' = 'red', '6' = 'green', '4' = 'blue'))

However, you can check that you get the same problem as before if you play with the labels instead of the values.  Does anyone know of a general rule as to when ggplot2 will recognize the named vectors or won't?  Is there a workaround?  I'm sure there's some easy thing I'm just missing here...

Cheers - thanks for the help
david.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Label reordering in color scales?
parts:
Hi,

Looking at scale-manual.r and scale-discrete-.r, I'm guessing that the
observed behavior is due to this bit,

has_names <- function(.) !is.null(names(.$output_set()))

The check for .has_names() does not seem to be present in scales other
than manual.


Best,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Label reordering in color scales?
parts:
Hi David,

It sounds like you're trying to set both the breaks and the labels
using a reasonable syntax, but it isn't supported by ggplot2. You
want:

scale_colour_discrete(breaks = c(1, 2), labels = c('One', 'Two'))

Hadley

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: Label reordering in color scales?
parts:
Great, thanks for the quick reply!

That might have done it, or at least I think I see how it works now.  So am I always ok if I enter the breaks and then the labels in the same order?  See below.

df <- data.frame(x = 1:9, y = 1:9, z = factor(rep(c('a','b','c'), each = 3)))

qplot(x, y, data = df, colour = z)

  

qplot(x, y, data = df, colour = z) +
  scale_colour_discrete(
    labels = c('a' = 'A', 'b' = 'B', 'c' = 'C')  
  )  # ok

  

qplot(x, y, data = df, colour = z) +
  scale_colour_discrete(
    labels = c('b' = 'B', 'a' = 'A', 'c' = 'C')  
  )  # mislabeled

  

qplot(x, y, data = df, colour = z) +
  scale_colour_discrete(
    breaks = c('b', 'a', 'c'),
    labels = c('b' = 'B', 'a' = 'A', 'c' = 'C')  
  )  # fixed     

qplot(x, y, data = df, colour = z) +
  scale_colour_discrete(
    breaks = c('b', 'a', 'c'),
    labels = c('a' = 'A', 'b' = 'B', 'c' = 'C')  
  )  # mislabeled again    

When I remove the names in the labels vector, I get the same results, as if they don't matter at all.  So then I suppose Baptiste's observation is right, and the names are only checked in scale_manual?

Thanks again,
david.
